sections.markdown:
## C — Safety and emissions inspections and required equipment: the two-year safety inspection, fees and certificates, exemptions, the equipment an inspection checks, license plates and plate lights, projections, towlines, the slow moving vehicle sign, studded tires, window tint, and emissions inspections
Knowledge domain: when a Missouri vehicle needs a safety inspection and how long it lasts, what inspections cost and how certificates work, which vehicles are exempt, the equipment checked in a safety inspection, the plates, lights, flags and signs Missouri law requires beyond the inspection, the seasonal and tinting limits, and where and when emissions inspections apply.

FACT_ID: sec16-F01 | anchor: A01
Many vehicles need a safety inspection before they can be registered or have their registration renewed, though some are exempt. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec16-F02 | anchor: A01
One safety inspection covers two registration years, unless the vehicle is sold in between. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec16-F03 | anchor: A01
Even model year vehicles are inspected when their registration expires in an even calendar year, and odd model year vehicles in an odd calendar year. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec16-F04 | anchor: A01
An official inspection station may charge no more than $12 for an inspection, or up to $10 for a motorcycle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec16-F05 | anchor: A01
A vehicle that passes receives a certificate of inspection as proof, and that certificate is good for 60 days. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec16-F06 | anchor: A01
A certificate from a Missouri dealer is good for 90 days when the inspection was done within 60 days before the purchase date. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec16-F07 | anchor: A01
Your registration renewal notice helps you tell whether your next renewal needs an inspection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec16-F08 | anchor: A01
Vehicles are exempt from safety inspection for the first ten years after their model year while they have under 150,000 miles, including vehicles with an out-of-state title. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec16-F09 | anchor: A01
All trailers are exempt from the safety inspection, as are vehicles with historic plates, vehicles sold for junk, salvage or rebuilding, and dealer-to-dealer sales. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec16-F10 | anchor: A01
Vehicles registered for 26,000 pounds or more for less than 12 months need no inspection if the registration is issued or renewed on or after April 1, even though the renewal notice lists one. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec16-F11 | anchor: A02
To pass, a vehicle's brakes must be in good working order. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-F12 | anchor: A02
A vehicle must have at least two working white headlights. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-F13 | anchor: A02
A vehicle must have at least two working red taillights plus reflectors that other drivers can see from 500 feet. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-F14 | anchor: A02
Turn signals and brake lights must work as the manufacturer originally installed them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-F15 | anchor: A02
The steering must not have too much play or bind. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-F16 | anchor: A02
Bald or mismatched tires are not allowed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-F17 | anchor: A02
A vehicle made after January 1, 1936 must have safety glass in every window. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-F18 | anchor: A02
The windshield's viewing area may not be badly broken, and nothing on it may reduce visibility except legally required stickers and informational signs on the factory-tinted upper strip. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-F19 | anchor: A02
A passenger car made after June 30, 1964 must have two sets of seat belts in the front seat. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-F20 | anchor: A02
A vehicle needs a working horn that other drivers and pedestrians can hear, and its windshield wipers must work. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-F21 | anchor: A02
A vehicle must have an attached exhaust pipe, muffler and tailpipe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-F22 | anchor: A02
A vehicle made after 1967 must have both an inside and an outside rearview mirror. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-F23 | anchor: A02
A non-diesel vehicle made after 1967 must keep its air pollution control devices as the manufacturer installed them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-F24 | anchor: A02
The fuel system, including lines, hoses, connections and tanks, must be firmly attached and free of leaks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-F25 | anchor: A02
Trucks registered for over 24,000 pounds that lack rear fenders must have mud flaps. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-F26 | anchor: A02
A passenger vehicle's bumpers may not be higher than 22 inches above the ground at their highest point. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-F27 | anchor: A03
License plates must be firmly fastened, fully visible and clean, and any plate frame must not cover any part of the plate. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec16-F28 | anchor: A03
If you get two plates, one goes on the front and one on the back; a trailer or motorcycle gets one plate, mounted on the back. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec16-F29 | anchor: A03
A truck licensed for more than 12,000 pounds gets one plate for the front, and a second plate, if requested, goes on the rear. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec16-F30 | anchor: A03
A white light must shine on the rear plate so it can be read from 50 feet. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec16-F31 | anchor: A03
A load extending more than five feet past the rear must carry a red flag or cloth at least sixteen inches square during the day and a red light from one-half hour after sunset until one-half hour before sunrise [A03].
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec16-F32 | anchor: A03
When towing another vehicle, the towline must keep the two vehicles within fifteen feet of one another, and both vehicles must display lights from one-half hour after sunset until one-half hour before sunrise [A03].
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec16-F33 | anchor: A03
From sunset to half an hour before sunrise, any vehicle going 25 mph or slower must show a clean, reflective slow moving vehicle sign on the rear, near the middle, at least four feet above the road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec16-F34 | anchor: A03
Studded snow tires are allowed only from November 1 to April 1. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec16-F35 | anchor: A03
Tint or sun-screening is allowed on side and rear windows, with the front door windows limited to no more than 65% light blockage. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec16-F36 | anchor: A03
Drivers living in St. Louis City and in St. Louis, St. Charles, Franklin and Jefferson counties must also get emissions inspections where they apply. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec16-F37 | anchor: A04
The emissions inspection is a two-year inspection on the same even and odd schedule as the safety inspection. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec16-F38 | anchor: A04
Vehicles must pass an emissions inspection when sold, whatever their model year, unless an exception applies. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec16-F39 | anchor: A04
New vehicles and first retail sales of titled vehicles during the model year and the next year are exempt at sale if the odometer reads under 6,000 miles. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0088]

Misconceptions: the inspection covers two registration years, but the certificate itself must be used within its short validity window; not every vehicle needs a safety inspection, since newer low-mileage vehicles and trailers are exempt; emissions inspections apply only in the listed St. Louis area, not statewide; studded tires are not legal outside the allowed dates.
Mnemonics: even with even and odd with odd for inspection years, just as for two-year registration; red flag by day, red light by night for a long load.
Glossary: certificate of inspection means the station's proof that the vehicle passed; model year means the year the manufacturer assigns to the vehicle; GVWR means gross vehicle weight rating; slow moving vehicle sign means the reflective rear emblem for slow vehicles; projection means a load overhanging the rear of the vehicle.
Dynamic facts: inspection fees, exemption ages and mileages, the emissions program counties and the window tint limit are set by law or rule and can change, and emissions program details must be refreshed from the Department of Natural Resources.
